methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Chips & Semiconductors (found 0 same-stage, 1 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 11 same-sector peers exist in Chips & Semiconductors, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
XMOS is a growth-stage semiconductor company that has raised over £200M to date. The chips & semiconductors sector contains 11 comparable companies—3 public (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private peers including Cerebras, SambaNova Systems, PsiQuantum, Etched, and Tenstorrent—though the peer universe presents methodological constraints for valuation.

The peer-median approach is not applicable here. Of the 11 same-sector peers identified, only one operates at an adjacent stage to XMOS's growth phase, and none meet the minimum threshold of three comparable companies needed for reliable median-based triangulation. The public comp set (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) spans dramatically different scales and business models, making sector-wide multiples unreliable. The private peer group offers richer stage alignment but lacks sufficient publicly disclosed financial metrics to extract consistent valuation multiples.

Without a sufficiently dense peer cohort meeting stage and tier similarity criteria, traditional comparable-company analysis cannot be applied with confidence. Valuation of XMOS would require alternative or supplementary methods—such as discounted cash flow analysis, venture capital return expectations, or precedent transaction analysis in the semiconductor funding market—none of which are present in the available data. Key uncertainties center on XMOS's revenue scale, profitability trajectory, and the specific technical defensibility of its IP relative to the fragmented private peer set. A robust valuation narrative requires either expanded financial disclosure from existing peers or methodological diversification beyond comparables.
